name: Moon
note: A waxing gibbous Moon provides both a full-disk framing reference and a visible terminator.

name: Pleiades
note: A wide cluster: compare how much context remains around its bright members.

name: Jupiter
note: The wide eyepieces show a small disk. The second stock eyepieces provide very different magnifications across kits.

name: Saturn
note: Compare the apparent scale of the ring system. Ring tilt is specific to this observing date.

name: Mars
note: Mars changes apparent size strongly with date; this is one disclosed scene, not a year-round size.

name: Venus
note: The phase and disk size depend on date. Twilight may dominate over the artificial skyglow setting.

name: Orion Nebula
note: The rendered nebula texture is a framing reference. Its color and contrast are not a visual-observing forecast.

name: Andromeda Galaxy
note: Its catalog extent is much larger than its bright core. Faint outer regions are strongly affected by real sky brightness.

name: Hercules Cluster
note: Compare angular scale; rendered texture is not proof that the same stars will resolve visually.

name: Ring Nebula
note: A compact target. A tiny or nearly invisible rendering at low power is meaningful; images are not automatically fitted to the object.

name: Beehive Cluster
note: A broad stellar target that complements the compact nebula and globular-cluster examples.
